html:
Oil has been pumped in Gabon since 1957, from fields around Port-Gentil on the coast, and from the 1970s it was the country's main source of income.

Before oil, Gabon lived on okoumé timber and some manganese. Output rose fast in the 1970s, Gabon joined OPEC in 1975, and with a small population it became one of the richest African states per head, paying for the Trans-Gabon Railway.

The money also held together the long rule of Omar Bongo, who used it to reward allies. Wealth stayed concentrated in Libreville and in few hands. Output peaked in the late 1990s, and falling oil prices and production have since pushed Gabon to look to timber, manganese and forest conservation.
sum: Oil has been pumped in Gabon since 1957, from fields around Port-Gentil on the coast, and from the 1970s it was the country's main source of income.
